edition_title: Interpretability advances as EU enforcement begins
intro: A busy day across research and policy. Two interpretability results landed alongside the first enforcement actions under the EU AI Act, while frontier labs published updated safety frameworks.

items.headline: New probe method reveals deceptive circuits in frontier models
items.summary: Researchers demonstrate a linear-probe technique that identifies deception-associated activations across three frontier models with 91% accuracy.
items.why_it_matters: A reliable deception signal would give evaluators a tool that does not depend on the model cooperating.

items.headline: Autonomy evals show capability jump in latest model generation
items.summary: METR's updated task suite shows the newest model generation completing 40% of long-horizon tasks that stumped predecessors.
items.why_it_matters: Autonomy benchmarks are the leading indicator regulators have said they will key thresholds to.

items.headline: EU opens first AI Act enforcement case against chatbot provider
items.summary: The European Commission opened proceedings against a mid-size chatbot provider over transparency obligations, the first case under the Act's GPAI rules.
items.why_it_matters: The case will set the template for how aggressively the Act's general-purpose provisions are enforced.

items.headline: Anthropic updates responsible scaling policy thresholds
items.summary: The revised policy adds explicit capability thresholds for autonomous replication and lowers the trigger for enhanced security measures.
items.why_it_matters: RSP revisions are the closest thing the field has to binding lab-side commitments.

items.headline: Zvi on the week in AI: enforcement theater or real teeth?
items.summary: A long analysis arguing the EU enforcement opening is more significant than skeptics allow, with a section on lab responses.
items.why_it_matters: Frames the debate the policy community will be having all week.
